# DNC plans 12 presidential primary debates starting in June
The Democratic National Committee is planning a dozen debates from June 2027 through March 2028.
Twelve debates. Up to 20 candidates split across two stages. And it all kicks off in June.
The Democratic National Committee on Monday [unveiled its initial plans](https://democrats.org/2028primary/) for the 2028 presidential primary debates, before a single major candidate has launched a campaign.
The DNC is employing a similar model to what it used in the last open primary in 2020, mapping out a dozen debates from June 2027 through March 2028. Five will be held in 2027, with seven to follow the next year. That includes debates in each of the six early primary states, all in 2028.
In a nod to how expansive the primary field is expected to be, the DNC said early debates could be held over two consecutive nights — and is capping participation at 20 candidates in total. Polling and grassroots fundraising are among the benchmarks that will help determine the qualifiers. The DNC said it would release more precise criteria for the first two debates, along with the dates and locations, in January.

ultimate.title: Democrats holding 12 debates in 2028 cycle, requiring candidates denounce 'dark money'
ultimate.snippet:
The Democratic National Committee announced on Monday that it will hold 12 primary debates in the 2028 presidential primary cycle, while also requiring candidates to denounce any "dark money" spending efforts on their behalf to participate.
The DNC said that five presidential primary debates will be held in 2027, with the first two in June and July, and seven will be held in 2028. Six of those will be held in 2028 in states that are holding primaries or caucuses in [the early window of the Democrats' presidential primary and caucus calendar](https://abcnews.com/Politics/dnc-set-finalize-controversial-2028-primary-calendar-elevating/story?id=135616869): South Carolina, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia.
The timing and number of debates are similar to the 2020 presidential cycle, where the party held 11 debates, with the first in June 2019; some debates were held across two nights as well.

"Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle," DNC chair Ken Martin wrote in a statement.

If a large number of candidates qualify for a debate -- a possibility given that many Democrats are expected to run -- some debates could be held across two nights "with qualifying candidates assigned one night per debate" and a maximum of 20 candidates across both nights, the DNC said.

One key rule candidates and their campaigns must follow to qualify is pledging to denounce any "dark money" spending in the primaries on their behalf. Dark money is spending on elections or other political contests in which the identities of the donors are obscured.
The pledge requires the campaigns to denounce and report to the DNC spending done by outside groups promoting the candidate or opposing their competitors, according to the DNC. Candidates that fail to denounce such spending will become ineligible to participate in the next scheduled debate.

ultimate.title: DNC plans to hold 12 debates for 2028 primary – with a new rule for Democrats who want in
ultimate.snippet:
The Democratic National Committee announced Monday it will hold [twelve debates](https://democrats.org/2028primary/) for the next presidential primary starting in June — and is adding a significant new condition for candidates to participate.
Candidates will have to sign a pledge to denounce super PAC and so-called “dark money” spending in the primary, a win for progressives who have long pushed for the party to crack down on big money in politics.

The first two debates will take place in June and July, and the DNC plans to hold the final debate in March 2028. Under the framework, there will be five debates in 2027 and seven in 2028.
The DNC also held 12 debates for the 2020 primary, the last time Democrats had an open nominating contest.
The DNC plans to announce more details for the 2028 primary debates, including dates, locations and media partners, in January. The DNC will also announce in January more criteria to qualify for the debates, including polling and fundraising thresholds.
The early debates may occur over two consecutive nights “in order to accommodate a potentially large field of candidates,” the DNC said. If that happens, each night’s lineup will be decided at random, with the total number of participants across both nights limited to 20 candidates.
The biggest change, though, is what the DNC is calling its Fair Campaign Practices Pledge. Under the pledge, candidates who want to join DNC debates must designate a representative who can complain to the committee about spending by a 501(c)(4) nonprofit — a type of group that does not have to disclose its donors — or a super PAC, which can raise and spend unlimited amounts of money from individuals and corporations. If the DNC agrees that the spending violates the pledge, it will ask candidates to provide a statement to the DNC denouncing the spending.
